Experimental macOS support, plus three features that help on every platform. Install with `pip install xc-xrunner`.

## macOS (experimental)

xrunner now runs on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or newer. It runs the Linux xrunner inside one Lima VM.

    brew install lima
    pip install xc-xrunner
    xrunner machine start
    xrunner run --rm alpine echo hi

- The first `xrunner machine start` creates an Ubuntu 24.04 VM with Rosetta. Your home folder, `/private/var/folders` and `/private/tmp` are shared into it at the same paths.
- `conda`, `shim`, `sandbox` and `machine` run on the Mac. Every other command runs in the VM, with the same exit code and output.
- `xrunner machine start|stop|status|shell|rm` manage the VM. The `XRUNNER_MACHINE_*` settings set its size and extra shared folders.
- This release was tested on Linux against a fake Lima only. It has not run on a real Mac yet. `scripts/mac_smoke.sh` runs the end-to-end checks on a Mac; please report what fails.

## All platforms

- **`XRUNNER_ENV_LAYER_DIR`** keeps env folder layers on another disk, while the environment record stays in the project. On a cluster, point it at node-local disk.
- **x86_64 images on ARM hosts.** With a Rosetta or qemu-x86_64 handler registered, an image list without an ARM image falls back to x86_64.
- **Pull-time architecture check.** An image the host cannot run now fails at pull time with a clear message, instead of failing later with "exec format error". An explicit `--platform` skips the check.
- **Conda shim on macOS ARM.** The shim pins micromamba 2.9.0 for `osx-arm64` as well as `linux-64`. A failed install on a Mac suggests `--platform osx-64`.
